newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM to return donations from health group.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM to return donations from health group.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto admitted to parliament on Tuesday he accepted political donations from an industry group after it had received a warning from the country's business watchdog.
"It was a careless thing to do on my part, and I will return the money," Hashimoto said at the Upper House budget committee in response to an opposition lawmaker's question on a newspaper report.
The donations were fully legal and properly reported but came from a firm that was part of a group of companies the Fair Trade Commission (FTC) warned was violating the Anti-trust Law.
The company was also affiliated to the Aya Welfare Group, a nursing home concern at the centre of a widening bribery scandal at the Health Ministry.
On Monday, Hashimoto told parliament he had not accepted money from the firm after the warning by the FTC was put into effect in June 1994.

However, the Japanese daily Mainichi Shimbun reported Hashimoto's fundraisers received two million yen ($17,600) in donations in July 1995 from a member company of the Japan Hospital Linen Supply Association, the paper said.
The FTC warned the association that its members were violating the Anti-trust Law with sales practices which excluded non-members from bids.

The company, which leases bedding to hospitals, is run by an associate of Aya Welfare Group head Hiroshi Koyama, who was arrested last month on suspicion of bribing health ministry officials in exchange for help getting government subsidies to build nursing homes.
The widening scandal in the health ministry has seen two officials arrested on suspicion of taking bribes from Koyama.
Vice Health Minister Nobuharu Okamitsu was arrested last week for allegedly receiving 60 million yen ($530,000) in bribes from Koyama.
In addition to the prime minister, Health Minister Junichiro Koizumi has admitted receiving political donations from lobby groups linked to the Aya Welfare Group. ($1=113 yen)
